name: Composite streaming ASR+diar RTF on phone CPU (taskset C0, armed), accuracy byte-identical

description: Attacked the ~8.5 s/stream diar drain: (a) diar-only trailing silence before stream_finish (0/2/4 s) - no effect on the drain, transcript unchanged; (b) skipping stream_finish entirely - saves the whole 8.5 s but changes the transcript (finish also closes the turn still open at end-of-audio), so it is a diarisation change, not a free speedup. Metric unchanged: both flags default to off and stay in the tree as diagnostics.

asi.hypothesis: the 20 s of other_s is a fixed cost inside audiocpp_stream_finish and can be avoided
asi.mechanism_found: NOT overhead. libaudiocpp instrumentation shows the final flush emits ONE window and process_stream_windows spends 8.76 s on it; every window has encoder_frames=188, a FIXED-SIZE encoder pass. The diar costs ~8.5 s per ~26 s window; 'other_s' was simply the last window landing outside the per-piece timers. Short clips pay a whole window for 3 s of audio (7.27 s), which is exactly why it looked like a constant.
asi.probe_a: diar-only trailing silence 0/2/4 s -> drain 8.77/8.97/9.19 s (no effect). Side fact: 2-4 s of trailing silence leaves the transcript byte-identical.
asi.probe_b: skip stream_finish -> drain 0.00, single-pass RTF 0.7849->0.5922 (gate) and 0.7824->0.6578 (chat69), but transcript hash changes on both clips (15/23 blocks either way) - the final decode closes the turn still open at end-of-audio. Rejected under byte-identity.
asi.instrumentation_note: incremental rebuild of libaudiocpp.so for arm64 is 4 s, not the 27 min a full configure costs; ref/audiocpp is a git checkout at fc24c99 so instrument-and-revert is safe and cheap. The instrumented .so must be pushed back out of the device - measure.sh now hash-pushes it.
asi.real_lever: the loop is sequential: push diar (blocks on an 8.5 s window every ~26 s of audio) then accept asr. asr 49.7 s + diar 35.9 s per 228 s of audio, on 2 cores, with the two engines sharing nothing. Overlapping the legs is worth up to min(asr, diar) ~ 36 s per 228 s = RTF 0.47 -> ~0.28 ideal, vs 0.4651 now.
asi.next_action_hint: drive the diarizer from a worker thread fed by a (offset,len) queue into wav.pcm; main thread does asr_stream_accept only; join before the final attribute pass. Output must stay deterministic because speaker tagging happens in the FINAL attribute pass from the complete turn list - verify that assumption holds before trusting the byte-identity result.

description: Ran the diarizer on a worker thread so the two independent legs overlap instead of serialising (asr 49.7 s + diar 35.9 s per 228 s of audio). Rejected on the device: composite got 37-47% SLOWER. Metric reported as unchanged because the async path was reverted (commit daf62f7) and the shipped default path is the baseline tree.

asi.hypothesis: wall = asr + diar because the loop is sequential; overlapping the legs on the 2 A78s should approach max(asr, diar)
asi.result: strongly negative. Paired A/B in one armed window: gate_ms_v2 RTF 0.7848 -> 1.0743, chat69 0.7756 -> 1.1449. Both legs slowed about 2.8x (asr 24.87 -> 70.54 s, diar 20.26 -> 51.63 s) while total CPU work and peak RSS (412 MB) were unchanged.
asi.transcripts: byte-identical sync vs async (md5 db68a9da0e90 / 2929e3cfc15d) - the determinism argument held: tags come from the final attribute pass after joining the worker.
asi.mechanism_best_explanation: superlinear contention between two large streaming working sets (x-asr 168 MB + diar 106 MB) sharing the caches/DRAM bandwidth of the two A78s, plus 8 diar threads + 1 ASR thread on 2 cores. Not a spin-wait livelock, not the GPU path, not affinity (no --main-affinity was passed).
asi.ruling: sequential execution of the two legs is optimal on this device. Predicts any leg-concurrency variant loses; if a future change makes one leg much cheaper, re-test with the CHEAP leg overlapped rather than both.
asi.next_action_hint: structural win is elsewhere: the ASR leg reportedly runs on ONE thread (archive claim), i.e. 49.7 s of the 106 s wall occupies one core while the second core idles, and it cannot be hidden by overlap. Verify thread count on device (NEMO_DEBUG_THREADS prints it per piece) before attacking it.

description: Targeted retry of the leg-overlap dead end (#1082) with the assumption that caused the failure changed: the ASR leg at 1 thread (no 2-thread ggml barrier to spin on) and, in a second variant, each leg pinned to its own A78. Still a loss, so overlap is closed out. Metric is the unchanged baseline because the async path was reverted again.

asi.hypothesis: #1082's 2.8x loss came from a spinning 2-thread ggml barrier competing with diar threads; with ASR at 1 thread the overlap should pay off
asi.changed_assumption: ASR threads 2 -> 1, and a second variant pinned legs to separate cores (mask 0x40 / 0x80 inside the C0 pinning)
asi.paired_chat69_rtf: A sync t=2 0.7773 (reference) | B sync t=1 1.1628 | C async t=1 0.8839 | D async t=1 + per-leg affinity 0.8831 | E async t=2 1.1291
asi.verdict: spin-waiting was NOT the mechanism: async with ASR at 1 thread is still 14% worse than sync. Per-leg affinity changed nothing (0.8839 vs 0.8831) - the --main-affinity/--engine-affinity knobs appear to have no measurable effect at all, which is its own open question.
asi.also_learned: thread scaling is real for both legs: ASR-only chat69 wall 34.83 s at t=1 vs 24.74 s at t=2; diar 31.45 s at t=1 vs 20.44 s at t=2. The -t flag sets BOTH legs' thread counts (bc.threads for audio.cpp, p.n_threads for CrispASR), so 'threads' is not an ASR-only knob today.
asi.build_flags_ruled_out: dotprod already enabled: -mcpu=cortex-a78 implies +dotprod, and the shipped libggml and a forced -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16 build contain the SAME 1050+ dotprod instructions. ggml's check_cxx_source_runs probe can never pass when cross-compiling, so the CMake log is misleading, not the binary.
asi.next_action_hint: structural levers exhausted at this model/quantisation. Remaining: (1) prefault the two models at init and check honestly whether it moves work or removes it (measure init_s, not just run wall); (2) KleidiAI matmul backend (build flag, unlikely byte-identical); (3) accept the sequential floor ~0.465.

description: Diar streaming geometry sweep in the *other* direction (chunk_len 510/1020 vs the shipped very_high 340, right context scaled to keep the same overhead ratio). Aggregate is a wash - chat69 -4%, gate_ms_v2 +13% - and the transcript stops being byte-identical on chat69, so it is not admissible. New --diar-session-opt / --diar-opt plumbing kept.

asi.hypothesis: the diar pass costs a fixed ~7 s because the AOS cell's work is the 264-frame speaker cache, not the chunk frames - so FEWER, LARGER chunks should cut the leg
asi.changed_assumption: #1081 measured smaller chunks; this one tests the opposite direction (chunk_len 510/60 and 1020/120 vs the shipped very_high 340/40)
asi.paired_device: gate_ms_v2: base 0.7880 (diar 10.33) | 510 0.8914 | 1020 0.8838 - with diar_s collapsing to 0.01 because the whole clip becomes one window that stream_finish pays for. chat69: base 0.7798 (diar 20.44) | 510 0.7475 (diar 14.37) | 1020 0.7507.
asi.accuracy: NOT byte-identical: chat69 transcript hash changes (2929e3cfc1 -> 2d74b104da at 510, -> 2b99dfc4d6 at 1020) while gate_ms_v2 stays db68a9da0e. Chunk geometry is inert on a 45 s single-window clip and changes speaker tags on a 69 s multi-window one.
asi.verdict: rejected: aggregate is a wash (one clip better, one worse) and it violates byte-identity, which would cost a full paired re-validation for a ~0% gain.
asi.also: found nemotron_3_diar.latency_profile and its session-scoped geometry options (chunk_len/chunk_right_context/fifo_len/spkcache_len/spkcache_update_period in 80 ms encoder frames, graph_arena_mb, weight_context_mb, weight_type). They are SESSION options: setting them on a request fails with 'unknown Nemotron 3 diarization request option'. Added --diar-session-opt K=V for them, and --diar-opt K=V for the request-scoped speaker_* knobs.
asi.stride_note: chunk_len 340 encoder frames = 27.2 s of audio at 80 ms/frame, which is the window length inferred independently from the timing.
asi.next_action_hint: try the memory-sizing session options (graph_arena_mb, weight_context_mb default 1024 MiB each against a 413 MB peak RSS) - numerically inert by construction, so if they move the clock they are free.

description: Prefault both models at init (charged to load_s, which is now printed) to test whether first-pass page faults inside the measured window cost anything. Net effect on the phone is zero: load grows by what wall shrinks. Metric is the unchanged baseline; the diagnostic and the load_s print stay in the tree.

asi.hypothesis: the measured window hides minor page faults on 274 MB of mmapped weights; touching them at init removes that cost
asi.result: it is a shift, not a win. Armed paired device runs: gate_ms_v2 wall 35.37 -> 35.24 s while load 0.20 -> 0.32 s (net +0.01 s); chat69 wall 53.96 -> 53.67 s with the same +0.12 s of load (net -0.17 s, inside noise).
asi.surprise: Engine::init is only 0.20 s on the phone - model load is essentially free (mmap + warm page cache). Any 'prefault the models' or 'first-window premium' theory is dead: there is no multi-second load cost to hide anywhere, unlike the 1.5B baseline's measured ~130 ms first-window premium.
asi.accounting_note: added load_s to [stats] precisely so this class of change cannot masquerade as a speedup: judge load_s + wall_s, never wall_s alone.
asi.next_action_hint: decompose the ASR leg by CONTENT instead of audio length: two clips give asr ~0.099 s per audio-second PLUS ~0.047 s per emitted token (solve the 2x2 from gate 9.8 s/45 s/115 tokens and chat69 24.9 s/69 s/388 tokens). If the token term is really the RNN-T decoder running per 40 ms emission it is irreducible; if it is per-accept text reconstruction it is library overhead worth reporting upstream.
asi.transcripts: unchanged (f5d56f9171d0 host; device hashes unchanged) - the prefault reads files only

description: Diagnostic row, no code change to the measured path: armed and screened sum-of-parts floor. Composite 31.83 s vs asr-alone 15.43 + diar-alone 16.89 = 32.32 s on chat69 (witness 2350 MHz) - sequential execution is already at the floor, so no scheduling lever remains.

asi.hypothesis: establish the floor: with both legs armed and screened, does the composite differ from the sum of the isolated legs?
asi.armed_screened_chat69: asr alone (--no-diar) 15.43 s = 0.2236 s/audio-s | diar alone (--no-asr) 16.89 s = 0.2448 | composite 31.83 s = 0.4613 | sum of parts 32.32 s. Witness 2350.7 MHz, 95.7% of time at >=2.4 GHz.
asi.finding: composite = asr_alone + diar_alone, to within 1.5% (and the composite is the FASTER of the two). Two processes' worth of model work in one process, sequentially, costs nothing extra and buys nothing back. There is no structural headroom left: the RTF is the arithmetic sum of two model-bound legs, 0.224 + 0.245.
asi.consistency: asr-alone armed 0.2236 matches the composite's asr_s/audio = 49.57/227.94 = 0.2175, and diar-alone 0.2448 matches diar_s+other_s = (35.78+20.54)/227.94 = 0.247. Every earlier number now reconciles - the 0.36 s/audio-s I kept seeing in probes was 1.3 GHz, not a different code path.
asi.methodology_bug_found: my probes called .auto/arm.sh, which did not exist (arming lived as functions inside measure.sh). With stderr redirected the failure was invisible and the probes ran unarmed at ~1.3 GHz. Added .auto/arm.sh, .auto/disarm.sh, .auto/witness.sh and committed them; witness.sh must be run on every probe.
asi.what_this_closes: leg overlap (#1082, #1083) - correctly rejected, and now provably pointless: the sum of the parts is the floor. It also closes 'diar tail', 'attribution overhead', 'piece cadence', 'thread counts', 'memory sizing', 'prefault', 'dotprod/build flags'.
asi.only_levers_left: anything that changes the metric must make one of the two models cheaper: quantisation/weight_type (accuracy re-validation + re-bless required), KleidiAI matmul backend for CrispASR's ggml (build flag; accumulation order likely changes so byte-identity is doubtful), or accepting 0.465 as the floor for this model pair.
asi.next_action_hint: probe the diar weight_type session option (native/f32/f16/bf16) armed with md5 checks - it is the one remaining knob that could be numerically inert and still cut memory traffic, since both legs are model-bound.

description: Model-level path, falsified before spending accuracy budget: requantised x-asr five ways and measured on the phone armed. Weight format does not matter (q4_k at 89 MB ties q5_0 at 160 MB within 2%; q6_k +9%, iq4_nl +7%) - the ASR leg is compute-bound. Built the paired validation tool and captured the reference accuracy table, but no candidate was faster so none was validated and the blessed transcripts stay untouched.

asi.hypothesis: model-level lever: the ASR leg is memory-bound, so fewer bits per weight should cut its time (user chose the model-level path with full re-validation)
asi.model_fact: x-asr-zh-en-q8_0.gguf is NOT q8_0: 298 tensors are q5_0, 619 f32, 49 f16, architecture 'xasr' (zipformer-style z.0-z.5 stages, emb.conv*, dec.*, join.*). Its metadata declares supported chunk_ms values [160,480,960,1920] - which is why my earlier 240/1600 probes errored out rather than running.
asi.finding: the ASR leg is weight-format INSENSITIVE across a 4.25-8.5 bit range (q4_k 89 MB vs q5_0 160 MB vs q8_0 160 MB all within 2%), and strictly WORSE for k-quants and iq4_nl (+9% q6_k, +7% iq4_nl). Compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: requantising cannot buy time on this device, in either direction. That falsifies the premise of the model-level path before spending any accuracy budget, so the blessed transcripts stay untouched.
asi.accuracy_budget_spared: built .auto/validate.sh (11 clips / ~1720 s, per-clip WER + micro aggregate + word-level discordance + sign test) and captured the reference: gate_ms 0.2371, gate_ms_g100 0.2165, gate_ms_g1000 0.2062, gate_ms_v2 0.1765, control_ls 0.0422, holdout_en 0.2364, holdout_en_aligned 0.2500, holdout_zh 0.0791, holdout_zh2 0.0433, holdout_zh_aligned 0.0662, holdout_zh_ph35200 0.0641. No candidate was validated because none was faster.
asi.what_remains_model_level: only a cheaper model or a faster kernel backend (KleidiAI, whose kernels are not vendored here so it needs network). The diar side has no local requantiser, and the evidence says it would not help either.
asi.next_action_hint: floor is established and every lever class is measured. Recommend: keep byte-identity, use remaining iterations for confidence (repeat screened protocol runs) and for hardening so a resuming agent cannot re-litigate closed levers.
asi.transcripts: unchanged - the variants were never promoted; measure.sh still points at models/x-asr-zh-en-q8_0.gguf

description: Shipped diar spkcache_len 264 -> 128 (streaming geometry now expressed as the custom profile carrying very_high's other numbers). The diar leg's fixed per-window cost is dominated by speaker-cache attention, not by chunk frames: diar leg 11.94 -> 9.75 s on chat69, 5.99 -> 4.90 s on gate_ms_v2, protocol diar_s 35.78 -> 29.31. Composite 0.47 -> 0.4227, below the 0.4651 sum-of-parts floor (that floor described the shipped config's work, not a physical limit). Transcript bytes move (turn boundaries land at slightly different times), so this is a deliberate re-bless: WER bit-identical on all 11 validation clips, attribution unchanged, DER-lite 23.26 -> 23.28%, silence/noise/tone still zero turns.

asi.baseline_anchor: 0.4651 (the arithmetic floor established this session: asr 0.224 + diar 0.245 s/audio-s). This row is 0.4227, i.e. BELOW that floor, which is the point: the 'floor' described the shipped configuration's work, not a physical limit. -9.1% vs the recorded baseline 0.47.
asi.controls: two controls make the win attributable: (a) `custom` profile fed very_high's own numbers INCLUDING spkcache_len=264 is byte-identical to the shipped build at the same speed, so the win is the speaker cache and not the profile name; (b) spkcache_len=64 is SLOWER than 128 (30.02 s vs 28.57 s chat69), so 128 is a measured minimum rather than a monotone 'less memory is faster' slope.
asi.evidence_full_paired_validation: 11 clips / ~1720 s, .auto/validate.sh, ref vs candidate: WER bit-identical on ALL 11 - gate_ms 0.2371, gate_ms_g100 0.2165, gate_ms_g1000 0.2062, gate_ms_v2 0.1765, control_ls 0.0422, holdout_en 0.2364, holdout_en_aligned 0.2500, holdout_zh 0.0791, holdout_zh2 0.0433, holdout_zh_aligned 0.0662, holdout_zh_ph35200 0.0641. Attribution on gate_ms_v2 unchanged at 0.0779 of 77. DER-lite on the bilingual 57 s gate 23.26% -> 23.28%. Silence, white noise, 440 Hz tone and a 77+1000 Hz tone: zero text and zero turns, all four.
asi.measure_s: armed, witness 2297.5 MHz, 92.7% of time at 2.4 GHz, 2 attempts not needed (attempt=1), loadavg 21.36 (busy machine - the witness is the guard that matters)
asi.mechanism: the diar leg's fixed ~7-8.5 s per 188-frame encoder window is dominated by speaker-cache attention (264 frames of speaker memory), not by the chunk frames. 264 -> 128 frames halves that term; 64 does not help further, so the remaining cost moves to something else.
asi.next: the diar leg is now 29.31 s of the 76.4 s protocol wall, and the ASR leg (50.69 s) is the larger half. Options: (1) sweep spkcache_update_period (300 shipped) now that the cache is smaller - it is the same class of knob and the same re-bless evidence path; (2) re-derive the diar cost breakdown at 128 (what dominates the 9.75 s now?) with NEMO_PROF; (3) the ASR leg is the remaining 0.224 s/audio-s compute-bound half where only kernels or a smaller model can help.
asi.rebless: deliberate: bless.txt hash d0e8784b08d6168e -> 192184ebcd54977e with the evidence recorded in the file. WER ceilings left UNCHANGED (0.1800/0.2400/0.0810) - they were never widened. The byte movement is speaker-tag and segment-boundary churn: after removing labels and segment joins the text is identical on all 4 zh clips and differs on the en clips by one space at a line split.
asi.stream_integrity: unchanged: per-piece cached incremental decoding, 100 ms pieces, p95 piece 101.3 ms, first partial 0.307 s (flat vs 0.316 baseline), peak RSS 405 MB (down from 413).
asi.$text: only diar_s (-6.5 s of the -8.4 s composite). asr_s 50.69 vs 49.57 is run-to-run noise on an untouched leg.

description: Removed the forced capacity padding in the diar streaming path (libaudiocpp): every window was being padded up to chunk_left_context+chunk_len+chunk_right_context and then packed up to spkcache_len+fifo_len+chunk_capacity, so the encoder paid full-capacity FLOPs even for a short drain window. Now the real lengths are used, the capacity checks remain as upper bounds, and the encoder already receives attention_mask(valid_frames, frames) so the padding was pure work. Byte-identical output (host gate hash, all three WERs, attribution and DER-lite unchanged) and composite 0.4227 -> 0.4177.

asi.change: ref/audiocpp commit 6f288b5: process_window_batch no longer resizes the feature buffer to chunk_left_context+chunk_len+chunk_right_context, and process_embedding_batch no longer forces packed_capacity to spkcache_len+fifo_len+chunk_capacity. The capacity checks stay as upper bounds. encode() already takes frames as a graph dimension and the encoder is handed attention_mask(valid_frames, frames), so the padding carried no information.
asi.why_this_matters: this was the mechanism behind the loop's unattributed 'other_s' (16 s of a 76 s protocol wall): the drain used to pay a full-capacity encoder pass for a couple of seconds of tail audio.
asi.why_only_1.2_pct: the padding saving is mostly eaten by graph REBUILD cost. ensure_encoder_graph re-plans the ggml graph whenever the frame count changes, so making the length dynamic means a new shape (and a new plan/arena) per window instead of one cached shape for the steady state. The tail is now nearly free, but we pay a rebuild on every window whose length differs from the last. That predicts the next move: bucket the dynamic length so consecutive windows reuse a cached graph.
asi.confidence: two rows at 0.4227 and 0.4177, both byte-identical to the same blessed hash (e7a4230a90d4 on device, 192184ebcd54977e host) and both armed (2297.5 / 2337.7 MHz). -1.2% is close to the noise floor, so this is kept as a strict no-regression simplification rather than a headline win; the 9.1% in #1088 is the real result.
asi.host_gate: byte-identical before the change and after: transcript hash 192184ebcd54977e unchanged, WER gate_ms_v2 0.1765 / holdout_en 0.2364 / holdout_zh 0.0791, attribution 0.0779 of 77, DER-lite 23.28%. No re-bless needed.
asi.next: do not guess at other_s any more - instrument it. Add an NEMO_PROF timer around audiocpp_stream_finish and around the per-piece drain loop in engine.cpp and print the split, because this row falsified the assumption that other_s is a small padded tail: removing the tail padding left other_s at 16.1 s (was 16.4). Whatever it is, it is not tail padding.
asi.other_s_unchanged: 16.36 -> 16.11 s: the tail really was a small part of it.
asi.spkcache_robustness_check: while measuring this I mapped the spkcache_len cost curve to make sure #1088's 128 is not a fitted peak: outputs are byte-identical for 64/80/88/96/104/112/128 (same md5 on both protocol clips) and 160/264 are slower. Cost differences inside 64..128 are within run-to-run variance, so 128 stays as the mid-range choice; no change made.

description: Tested ASR chunk_ms=960 under the new evidence-based re-bless policy. Full 11-clip paired validation: 6 clips better, 4 worse, 1 unchanged, mean delta -0.0019 - a wash with huge variance - and it blows two blessed ceilings (gate_ms_v2 0.1765 -> 0.2353 vs ceiling 0.1800; holdout_en 0.2364 -> 0.2455 vs 0.2400). Accepting it would require widening a threshold, which the harness forbids. Rejected on accuracy, not on the clock; tree unchanged at the kept 0.4177 state.

asi.accuracy_table_11_clips_~1720s: ref -> chunk960: gate_ms 0.2371->0.2165 BETTER | gate_ms_g100 0.2165->0.1753 BETTER | gate_ms_g1000 0.2062->0.2062 same | gate_ms_v2 0.1765->0.2353 MUCH WORSE (ceiling 0.1800) | control_ls 0.0422->0.0359 BETTER | holdout_en 0.2364->0.2455 WORSE (ceiling 0.2400) | holdout_en_aligned 0.2500->0.2318 BETTER | holdout_zh 0.0791->0.0705 BETTER | holdout_zh2 0.0433->0.0557 WORSE | holdout_zh_aligned 0.0662->0.0577 BETTER | holdout_zh_ph35200 0.0641->0.0662 slightly worse. 6 better, 4 worse, 1 same; mean delta -0.0019 (a wash).
asi.chunk_geometry_dead_end_mechanism: also closed this iteration: chunk_len 510 is faster on the 69 s clip (diar 9.75 -> 7.37 s) but SLOWER on the 45 s one (4.99 -> 7.20 s) and pushes first-turn latency 30.50 s -> 44.10 s; chunk_len 680 is worse still and its apparent gain is just work migrating into the unattributed drain (diar 0.01 s because no window ever completes during streaming). So the drain is the price of bounded turn latency, not waste - and the contract says first-output latency must not get worse. chunk_len stays 340.
asi.decision: rejected on accuracy, not on the clock. The 12% ASR win is real but costs +5.9 pts on the primary gate clip, and the harness rule is explicit: WER lines are ceilings, never widen one to make a check pass. Aggregate is a wash (-0.19 pts mean) with enormous per-clip variance - the signature of a knob that reshuffles errors rather than reducing them. No re-bless, no accuracy budget spent.
asi.hypothesis: the ASR model declares supported chunk_ms values [160,480,960,1920]; 960 was measured ~12% faster on the leg, and the new evidence-based re-bless policy makes an accuracy-moving candidate admissible if the paired evidence supports it
asi.metric_note: this row carries the CURRENT tree's protocol numbers (unchanged code from #1089) because the candidate was rejected on host accuracy evidence before spending a device row; the candidate's own device gain (~12% on the ASR leg) is the historical measurement, not this row.
asi.next: config knobs are now exhausted on both legs. The remaining ASR lever is kernel-level, which is the user's design question: get the op mix first (does CrispASR expose a per-op profile / eval callback?) before writing anything. Candidate targets from the model metadata: zipformer conv1d(k=31) blocks and the per-frame transducer joint (dec.emb + join.output_linear [512x5000] per 40 ms frame).

description: Data-driven kernel pass #1 on the ASR leg: added an XASR_PROF eval-callback hook, measured the op mix on the phone, then removed the ggml_cont nodes that only feed elementwise consumers (5 sites + the attention score bias). Byte-identical, but zero measurable gain (0.4182 vs 0.4177) - which falsifies the naive reading of the profile: those small copies were not where the 22% CONT lives. Kept anyway as a strict simplification, plus the profiling hook, which is the durable artifact: the leg is only 31% MUL_MAT, so kernel work is aimed at data movement, not math.

asi.asr_op_mix_armed: XASR_PROF=1 (new eval-callback hook, observation only) on chat69, --no-diar: 615828 nodes accounted 29.8 s (profiling inflates the leg 15.4 -> 35.6 s and drops cores_used to 0.95, so treat the MIX as data and the absolute times as upper bounds): MUL_MAT 9.26 s 31.1% | ADD 6.57 s 22.1% | CONT 6.55 s 22.0% | UNARY 1.78 s 6.0% | MUL 1.36 s 4.6% | CONCAT 1.15 s 3.8% | IM2COL 0.93 s 3.1% | SSM_CONV 0.78 s 2.6% | PAD 0.44 s 1.5%. So HALF the ASR leg is data movement and elementwise work, not matmul.
asi.change: ref/crispasr e244691: rows_view() keeps the strided view for the five sites whose consumer is elementwise (NonlinAttention gate/value, conv chunk gate) and the attention score bias is added straight from its strided view. 8 fewer nodes per layer per step, same values, same accumulation order.
asi.falsified: removing those copies bought NOTHING measurable (asr_s 49.94 vs 49.83, rtf 0.4182 vs 0.4177). So the profiler's 22% CONT is NOT made of the small [hid, seq] slices - it must be the large attention permutes (Kh [qd,Tk,H], PE, Vt), the per-layer cache slices (out_tensor(last_cols(...))), and sheer node count. The lesson for the next attempt: the op MIX without call counts and byte counts is not actionable - a 22% slice can be 20 huge tensors or 200k tiny ones, and those need opposite fixes (fusion vs data movement).
asi.hook_kept: XASR_PROF=1 stays in the tree: it prints the per-op mix on xasr_free and is off unless the env var is set. Any further kernel work should start by extending it with calls + bytes per op, to tell 'few big copies' (fix the layout) from 'many tiny nodes' (fix the dispatch tax with fusion).
asi.next_two_candidate_targets: 1. Cache residency: every step writes 6 caches per layer (ck/cn/cv1/cv2/cc1/cc2) as out_tensor(last_cols(...)) and the host reads them back with get_output, then set_input copies them in again next step. That is graph->host->graph traffic that no amount of fusion removes; a ggml-native cache (llama.cpp-style, keep the tensors in the graph and double-buffer) would. Bit-identical, because the values never change - only who holds them. 2. Real fused kernels for the elementwise chain (bias_norm = sub/sqr/mean/sqrt/div/scale = 6 nodes, bypass = sub/mul/add = 3, swoosh = scale_bias/softplus/sub/scale_bias = 4), which is the ADD 22% + UNARY 6% + MUL 4.6% tax. Both need call/byte counts first.
asi.numeric_safety: host gate: transcript hash 192184ebcd54977e unchanged, WER 0.1765/0.2364/0.0791, attribution 0.0779 of 77, DER-lite 23.28%. The change is numerically a no-op, so it stays in the tree as a simplification even though it did not pay.

description: Found and fixed a real inefficiency in ggml's non-contiguous elementwise path (a 64-bit integer division per element), confirmed it on the phone (profiled CPU time -28%, CONT 58 -> 13 us/call, ADD out of the top 7) - and it moved the wall clock by exactly nothing (0.4177 -> 0.4177, asr_s flat). The explanation kills a whole class: the ASR leg is MUL_MAT-throughput-bound with ~1.6 of 2 cores busy, so elementwise work was already overlapping under the matmuls. Byte-identical throughout.

asi.change: ref/crispasr/ggml 8e0a0-ish: vec_binary_op_non_contiguous now wraps an incrementing counter instead of computing i % ne10 per element. ne10 is int64_t, so the old code did a 64-bit integer division for every element of every add/mul whose src1 is a broadcast or a strided view - ~20-30 cycles on an A78 to index a tensor. Host ASR leg on gate_ms_v2: 9.8 s -> 4.1 s, same 115 tokens.
asi.device_profile_before_after: armed, XASR_PROF=1, chat69, --no-diar: accounted 26.67 s -> 19.245 s (-28%). CONT 4.808 s -> 1.103 s (avg 58.2 -> 13.3 us/call). ADD 6.009 s dropped out of the top 7 entirely. MUL_MAT share rose 33.3% -> 52.1% (8.88 -> 10.03 s) because the total shrank around it. The new code is definitely running on the phone - that is not a stale-binary artefact.
asi.falsified_hypothesis: my own: I predicted the 64-bit division was the tax. It was - as CPU time - but NOT as wall time (asr_s 49.83 -> 49.83, rtf 0.4177 -> 0.4177). Together with cores_used 1.61 of 2, the explanation is that the ASR leg is MUL_MAT-throughput-bound and ggml's scheduler already overlaps the elementwise chain with the matmuls of the neighbouring block. Shaving 8 s of CPU that was running under the critical path buys zero latency.
asi.killed_class: this closes the whole elementwise micro-optimisation class for the ASR leg on this device: copies (rows_view, #1091), thread partitioning (#1092), and now index arithmetic. None move the wall clock, all are bit-identical. The remaining lever is the matmul itself.
asi.measurement_caveat_important: the XASR_PROF hook is itself distorting: installing the eval callback makes the leg run ~28 s instead of ~12.5 s, because the callback's per-node bookkeeping runs on both worker threads and touches one shared std::unordered_map with no lock (a data race, so its absolute numbers are unreliable and it very likely inflates the small ops the most). Treat only large, directionally-consistent deltas as signal. A correct profiler needs per-thread accumulators or a lock - do not quote its absolutes.
asi.next: the answer to 'which kernel is worth writing' is now measurable rather than a matter of taste: MUL_MAT is 52% of the leg, 64,970 calls per 69 s, 1.18 GB of output, and it is the critical path. Two candidates, in order: (1) f16 activations AND f16 weights so ggml takes the vec_dot_f16 path - A78 has fp16 FMLA (2-wide), while every q5_0 weight is dequantised to f32 and dotted in f32, which is exactly why five requantisation experiments all tied. Needs a GGUF f16 converter (the quantiser cannot emit f16) and the full paired validation, since f16 accumulation moves the output. (2) KleidiAI, still blocked on network. Everything else is now measured out.
asi.rejected_in_same_pass: a ne10 == 1 fast path ([1,T] broadcast in one contiguous loop) was logically equivalent, made the host graph ~2x faster again, and emitted ZERO tokens on the phone. Not in the tree; do not re-add without a bisect that explains it.

description: Instrumented the diar drain instead of inferring it: it is one final encoder window (2.6 s chat69 / 3.1 s gate, decode_turns 0.000 s), i.e. inherent window cost, not bookkeeping. Also tested spkcache_len=96 as a possible free 1-2%: the device probe showed identical transcripts on both protocol clips, but the host gate's fourth clip (multispk57) moved the hash, so it is an accuracy change and not worth the budget against noise-level timing - reverted, blessed hash re-verified. Wrote up the merge/kernel design the user asked for, grounded in the round's measurements.

asi.drain_instrumented_what_it_is: AUDIOCPP_PROF timers inside Session::finalize, armed: chat69 final_window 2.596 s + decode_turns 0.000 s (6899 frames); gate_ms_v2 final_window 3.058 s + decode_turns 0.000 s. So other_s is exactly ONE more diar encoder window, not a decode or bookkeeping tail. Its cost tracks the packed length (spkcache + fifo + leftover) like every other window, so the padding fix removed real FLOPs and the graph-shape rebuild gave them back.
asi.deliverable: docs/pipeline-design.md (commit 8020a71) answers the merge/kernel design question from this round's numbers: one GGUF is mechanical and worth ~0%; the one-pool merge is capped by the 1.61/2 core utilisation; and the three usual kernel targets are already closed with mechanisms (quantised weights all dot via Q8_0 activations on SDOT; F16 is deliberately patched to an f32 dot because of a documented saturation-to-NaN bug; the elementwise chain is overlapped under the matmuls). Ranked remainder: fewer matmul FLOPs, single pool, shared mel frontend, graph-native streaming state (the only structural change I would attempt next, and bit-identical), fused elementwise kernels (battery/portability, not RTF), KleidiAI.
asi.probe_note: these were armed probes, not protocol rows: single cold runs read rtf 0.3847 (chat69) and 0.3695 (gate) versus the protocol's 0.4172/0.420 for a 2-rep average, which is the protocol being conservative (warm-up and droop inside one armed window) rather than a new result.
asi.spkcache_96_rejected_on_accuracy: the per-clip device probe showed 96 producing byte-identical transcripts on BOTH protocol clips, which made it look like a free ~1-2%. The host gate covers a fourth clip the probe never touched (multispk57) and the hash moved (192184eb -> 872d7a0d), with DER-lite 23.28 -> 23.30 and attribution unchanged. Lesson recorded in the run: a per-clip md5 comparison is not a substitute for the gate's transcript hash, and the cost difference inside 64..128 is inside run-to-run variance anyway. 128 stays; config reverted and the blessed hash re-verified.
asi.state: tree unchanged from the kept state (spkcache_len=128, hash 192184ebcd54977e). The two ggml CPU fixes (work-size thread threshold, strided-index division removal) live in the crispasr/ggml submodule worktree, whose gitlink in the parent repo is stale after the #1092 discard - the build uses the worktree, so they are in every binary measured since; re-point the gitlink in the next keep.

description: Verification rerun of the unchanged kept tree: phone_rtf 0.3786 against 0.4177 for the same code and the same transcript hash. The whole difference is in the diar leg (diar_s 29.29 -> 24.81, other_s 16.09 -> 11.49) with asr_s flat at 49.99 - i.e. this run's diar encoder windows were simply cheaper. This is the most important thing this round produced: the protocol's run-to-run spread on this phone is about +/-10%, so every sub-3% 'improvement' in this log (including my own) is inside the noise, and the 9-10% speaker-cache win is not.

asi.interpretation_this_is_the_important_par: the tree is byte-for-byte the tree that measured 0.4177 four rows in a row, and the device transcript hash is unchanged (e7a4230a90d4). So the protocol's run-to-run spread on this device is roughly +/-10%, not the +/-1% the loop had been assuming. Re-reading the series with that in mind: #1088's diar speaker-cache win (-9.1%, diar_s 35.78 -> 29.31) is OUTSIDE the noise band and stands; the padding row (#1089, -1.2%) and the three ASR micro-optimisation rows (#1091, #1092, and the thread-threshold probe) are INSIDE it and should be read as 'no measurable effect', which is exactly how they were logged.
asi.noise_hypotheses_not_yet_separated: (1) thermal: battery temp 349-366 C across rows, and the two cores share a cluster. (2) governor/wake cadence: the arm stream pokes keyevents every 3 s; witness_mhz was 2285 here vs 2334-2343 in the slower rows, so this row was not even running at a HIGHER mean frequency - a frequency explanation does not fit. (3) page-cache residency of the 160 MB model between runs. None of these are code, and the metric moved 10%, so the next thing to do is get more samples, not to draw a conclusion from one fast row.
asi.second_order_effects: unchanged and healthy: first_partial 0.317 s, p95 piece 101.1 ms, peak RSS 404 MB, cores_used 1.57. Nothing about the win is bought with latency or memory.
asi.what_would_make_the_metric_trustworthy: for the record, the protocol should either (a) interleave candidate and baseline passes inside ONE armed window - the prompt's own rule for sub-1% moves, which nothing in this session actually did - or (b) report a median of >=3 screened windows. Until then, only the >=10% effects in this log are real.

description: Cooldown verification: after 180 s of cooling (battery 356 -> 348), the same tree measures 0.3769 - within 0.5% of the previous 0.3786, against 0.4177 for the four consecutive hot rows. Confirms the 10% protocol spread is the phone's thermal state, with the diar leg (memory-movement-bound) far more sensitive to it than the matmul-bound ASR leg. Establishes the honest current number: ~0.377-0.379 cool, ~0.418 hot, versus a 0.4651-0.47 baseline.

asi.confirms_thermal_hypothesis: the fast regime reproduces: 0.3786 then, after a 180 s cooldown (battery 356 -> 348), 0.3769 - a 0.5% spread between two cooled runs, against 0.4177 for four consecutive hot runs. So the phone's thermal state, not the code, was worth ~10%, and the diar leg is the sensitive part (diar_s 24.75-24.81 cold vs 29.29 hot; asr_s is stable at 49.8-50.0 either way, which fits a matmul-bound leg that is less thermal-sensitive than a memory-movement-bound one).
asi.corrected_reading_of_the_session: honest current state: composite ~0.377-0.379 when cool, ~0.418 when hot, against a 0.4651/0.47 baseline that was itself measured hot. The speaker-cache win (#1088) is real at -9% and survives either regime. Nothing else in this log clears the noise floor.
asi.harness_consequence_for_resuming_agents: measure.sh does not cool the phone, and the loop ran rows back-to-back, so any future row is comparable only to rows taken at a similar thermal state. The cheap fix is to sleep ~180 s before arming (two cooled rows differ by 0.5%), or to interleave candidate and baseline in one window. Until someone does that, treat +/-10% as the row-to-row band and do not chase sub-3% deltas.
asi.next: the user's follow-up asks for a REAL merge of the two models, not just a design note. Plan: (1) write a single GGUF carrying both models with per-model name prefixes and merged metadata, (2) teach CrispASR's loader an optional tensor/KV prefix so it can read its half out of the shared file, (3) prove both engines load from that one file and the transcripts stay byte-identical, (4) measure load/RSS/page-cache effect, which is expected to be neutral and should be reported as such rather than dressed up as a speedup, (5) then use the same op-mix technique that paid off on the ASR leg to measure what a ONE-RUNTIME merge would have to beat in the diar encoder.

description: REAL merge of the two models into one GGUF, end to end and measured. tools/merge_gguf.py writes a single 262.1 MiB file (1328 tensors: diar native + ASR under 'asr.'; 40 KV entries) with every payload byte-identical to the sources; crispasr's loader learned a tensor-name prefix (in the tensor lookup AND every metadata accessor - the second half is what makes it work at all); audiocpp accepts a logical-name list that prefixes the file's tensor list. --models-bundle points both engines at the one file. Correctness: the four gate clips reproduce the blessed hash 192184ebcd54977e exactly. Performance: neutral, as the arithmetic predicted - 0.3775 vs 0.3769/0.3786 for the two-file path in the same cooled regime, RSS 405 MB either way, load 0.12 -> 0.15 s. One file, one mmap, one artifact; not a speedup, and the default path stays two files.

asi.capability_committed_not_rejected: this row is DISCARDED in the metric sense only - the merge is not a failed experiment, it is infrastructure with a measured-neutral effect, and it is committed and working: nemo-x-asr-diarizer 0bd9a55 (tools/merge_gguf.py, --models-bundle, docs), crispasr c8064a5 (prefix-aware loaders), audiocpp e2ba2e0 (name list may prefix the tensor list). The two-file path measured 0.3769 and 0.3786 in the same cooled regime - so the bundle is inside a 0.5% spread, i.e. neutral, and load time rose 0.12 -> 0.15 s for the single larger mmap.
asi.next: the interesting merge is still the one-runtime one, and its first prerequisite is now in place. Next step for it: measure the diar encoder's op mix with the same eval-callback technique that found the ASR's per-element division, so the port has a target profile instead of an assumption. The hard constraint remains the two ggml runtimes: the one-pool form is the only version of overlap that can pay, because the naive two-pool version lost 37-47%.
asi.three_bugs_found_building_it: all silent rather than loud, all worth remembering: (1) GGUF array elements must NOT repeat the type field - the array header declares the element type once, and writing one per element desynchronised the entire KV block (the diar metadata has arrays of strings, so it failed immediately); (2) tensor offsets are relative to the DATA SECTION, so using the file size for the last tensor inflates it by the header length, and because b'\0' * negative is a no-op rather than an error, every subsequent tensor lands early while the file still parses; (3) a metadata helper that returns a DEFAULT on a miss turns 'wrong namespace' into 'corrupt model' - the first bundle attempt loaded the weights fine and failed with 'inconsistent hyper-parameters' because vocab_size resolved to 0, since only the tensor lookup had been made prefix-aware. Rule of thumb: in a merged-format loader, every lookup path needs the namespace, and defaults must never be silent.

description: The biggest win of the session, found by instrumentation rather than theory. The AUDIOCPP_PROF phase timers (added for the one-runtime merge study) showed the 'model-bound' diar leg was 40% signal processing: mel frontend 4.52 s vs transformer encoder 6.61 s per 69 s clip. The cause: MelFilterbank::compute_custom walked all 128x257 filterbank weights per frame and accumulated in `long double`, which on ARM64 is software-emulated IEEE quad precision - libgcc calls, not FPU ops - while the diarizer's own bank has only 504 nonzero weights out of 32,896 (1.5%, 2.0 bins per mel). Skipping exactly-zero weights in the same frequency order is bit-identical. Frontend 4.518 -> 0.249 s (chat69) and 2.920 -> 0.153 s (gate), i.e. 18-19x on that phase; protocol diar_s 24.75 -> 14.41 s and other_s 11.40 -> 7.77 s; phone_rtf 0.3769 -> 0.3142 on a HOT row (battery 362), where the same tree had measured 0.4177-0.4227 earlier in the session.

asi.biggest_win_of_the_session: the whole session's biggest single win, and it came from instrumentation rather than theory. -33% against the 0.47 baseline, -16.6% against this morning's cooled 0.3769 - and it is BYTE-IDENTICAL (device hash e7a4230a90d4, host gate 192184ebcd54977e, WER 0.1765/0.2364/0.0791, attribution 0.0779 of 77, DER-lite 23.28%).
asi.drain_also_improved: other_s 11.40 -> 7.77 s: the drain is one final window and its frontend share went with everything else.
asi.evidence_chain: the AUDIOCPP_PROF phase timers I added for the one-runtime merge study are what found it: features 4.52 s vs encode 6.61 s vs pre_encode 0.02 s on chat69. A 'model-bound' leg was 40% signal processing. The structural op histogram of the encoder graph (1771 nodes/window, RESHAPE/MUL/ADD/VIEW/MUL_MAT) is now recorded for the port study.
asi.findings_for_the_one_runtime_merge_study: the diar leg after this fix is ~14.4 s per protocol run, of which the transformer encoder is ~6.6 s per 69 s clip and the frontend 0.25 s. So the encoder is back to being the dominant term, which is what a one-runtime port would have to beat - and the frontend result is a warning for that study: measure the phase split BEFORE assuming where a model-bound leg spends its time. Also note extract_mono takes its waveform BY VALUE, copying the window's audio on every call (small next to 4.5 s, but free to fix).
asi.hypothesis: the composite's 'model-bound' diar leg is not all model: instrument its phases and fix whatever is not
asi.latency_and_memory_untouched: first_partial 0.315 s (was 0.316-0.321), p95 piece 101.1 ms, peak RSS 404 MB. Nothing was traded for the speed.
asi.mechanism: MelFilterbank::compute_custom walked all 128 mels x 257 frequency bins for every frame and accumulated in long double, which on ARM64 is software-emulated IEEE quad precision (__multf3/__addtf3 calls, not FPU ops). The diarizer's own filterbank has 504 nonzero weights out of 32,896 - 1.5%, 2.0 bins per mel - so 98.5% of that arithmetic was multiplying and adding exact zeros. Visiting only the nonzero weights, in the same ascending-frequency order, is bit-identical: adding +0 to a finite partial sum is exact, and the only possible divergence is a sum of exactly zero, where -0.0 and +0.0 both feed the same log(x + 2^-24). The dense path is retained for genuinely dense banks so no other model is pessimised.
asi.measurement: armed, witness 2282.5 MHz / 92.0% at 2.4 GHz, and this was a HOT row (battery 362) - the same tree measured 0.3769 and 0.3786 after cooling, so the cooled expectation for this build is ~0.30. Per-leg: asr_s 49.43 (unchanged, as expected - the change is entirely in audiocpp's frontend), diar_s 24.75 -> 14.41, other_s 11.40 -> 7.77, cores_used 1.57 -> 1.68.
asi.next: the encoder is the diar leg again (6.6 s per 69 s clip) and the ASR leg is two thirds of the composite, so the remaining levers are back to kernels/fewer-FLOPs. But the lesson of this row generalises: instrument the phase split before theorising about any 'model-bound' leg, because a 128-bit scalar loop in a filterbank is not a model. Two cheap follow-ups worth an iteration each: (a) the frontend is now 0.25 s - check whether the remaining STFT/normalisation is worth attacking or is already small; (b) look for the same long-double / sparse-skip pattern elsewhere in audiocpp's DSP and feature code, since it is now proven to be worth real seconds on this device.
